clue.text: Pays up somehow to secure right ancient document

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the rearranged letters close round the abbreviation for right
somehow says the letters of pays up get there by some unstated route, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone grudgingly hands over cash to get hold of an antique manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Papyrus is the reed paper of ancient Egypt, and the word also names a scroll or text written on it.

clue.text: Ready, in Spain, to take position in plant

indicators.note: the plant takes in the word for position, holding it inside

parts.note: a pea is a climbing plant
to set is to position

explanation.surface: Someone is prepared, in Spain, to settle into a job at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready looks like an adjective, but it is the noun: readies is British slang for cash, and the peseta was Spain's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was Spanish cash before the euro, and ready money means cash in hand.

clue.text: Course holder's line in sales pitch

indicators.note: in places the line inside the salesman's talk

parts.note: patter is a salesman's glib talk
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A note on what the person running a course says when selling it.
explanation.walkthrough: Course means a part of a meal, not a training class.
explanation.definitionFit: A platter is a large serving dish on which a course of a meal is brought to the table.

clue.text: Send down girl who's out of practice, say

indicators.note: say tells us to speak the description and listen for a single word

parts.note: out of practice is rusty, and the girl is Kate

explanation.surface: Expelling a girl whose skills have slipped.
explanation.walkthrough: Send down here is the British university term for suspending or expelling a student.
explanation.definitionFit: To rusticate a student is to suspend them from Oxford or Cambridge, sending them away to the country.

clue.text: Cheat, providing limited peal of bells

parts.note: short means restricted or lacking
in bell-ringing a change is one ordering of the bells in a peal

explanation.surface: Someone cheated by a church offering only a brief ringing of the bells.
explanation.definitionFit: To short-change is to give too little money back, and more widely to swindle someone.

clue.text: Service provided by Jeeves personally

indicators.note: the letters are supplied by the words that follow, sitting inside them unchanged

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Wodehouse's valet Jeeves takes it upon himself to conduct a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeeves is P. G. Wodehouse's famously capable valet; the name hides the start of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespers is the evening prayer service of the Christian church, said or sung around sunset.

clue.text: The vehicle in front

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a covered motor vehicle for goods

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one vehicle at the head of a queue; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a delivery truck and is also short for vanguard, the foremost part of a moving force.

clue.text: Evidence almost overwhelms scholar, one of 22's set

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
in a down clue, to overwhelm is to sit on top, so the shortened word comes first

parts.note: a sign is evidence of something
MA is the Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Proof very nearly swamps an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition cross-refers to 22 down, whose answer is a Greek letter, so this is another of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, the same set as theta.

clue.text: Academic point about it is offensive

parts.note: E is East, a compass point

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the offensive word goes round it

parts.note: rude means offensive
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scholarly point about something is found insulting.
explanation.walkthrough: Academic looks like the subject of the sentence but is the definition, used as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudite means deeply learned and scholarly, which is the adjective sense of academic.

clue.text: Some Africans prosecute Europeans coming in

indicators.note: the Europeans come into the word for prosecute, ending up inside it

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action
Danes are people of Denmark

explanation.surface: Some Africans take legal action against Europeans arriving in their country.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudanese is the plural noun for people from Sudan, an African country.

clue.text: E.g. Shakespeare's blue cotton cloth

parts.note: Shakespeare is the Swan of Avon, so he is an example of a swan; with the possessive
blue and down both mean sad or low in spirits

explanation.surface: A note that Shakespeare favoured a blue cotton fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Jonson called Shakespeare the Sweet Swan of Avon, the river at Stratford, which is why he stands for a swan here.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansdown is also the name of a thick cotton fabric with a soft raised nap, like the feathers it is named after.

clue.text: Glutton dispatches servant to get fruit

indicators.note: to dispatch someone is to send them away, so the servant leaves the word for a glutton

parts.note: a gourmand is a greedy eater
a man is a manservant

explanation.surface: A greedy diner sends the waiter off to fetch some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourd is the hard-skinned fruit of plants such as the squash and bottle gourd family.

clue.text: Less than half the ice-cream for all the performers

indicators.note: only a portion short of half of the dessert's name is kept, read from its start

parts.note: its first five of twelve letters are kept

explanation.surface: Someone gets less than half a share of the ice cream meant for the whole cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is the musical direction that the whole ensemble plays together, Italian for all of them.

clue.text: Army's obsession initially narks islander

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve; with the possessive
a mania is a fixation

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the first letter of narks

explanation.surface: The army's fixation is beginning to irritate a man from an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tasmanian is a native of Tasmania, the large island state south of mainland Australia.

clue.text: Instrument amplifying beat given by organ

definitions.text: Instrument amplifying beat given by organ

parts.words: Instrument amplifying beat given by organ
parts.note: surface reading: a musical device boosting the rhythm played on a church organ

parts.words: Instrument amplifying beat given by organ
parts.note: setter's reading: a medical device making the pulse of the heart audible

explanation.walkthrough: Organ suggests the keyboard instrument and beat a musical rhythm; the organ is the heart and the beat its pulse.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's listening device carries the sound of the heart and lungs to the ears.

clue.text: State of excitement is not so new in parts of these bars

indicators.note: in places the comparative phrase inside the rearranged bars
the following words are broken into parts and rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged and split
not so much means less
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A comment that some excitement is less fresh within sections of music.
explanation.walkthrough: Parts of is doing double duty: the rearranged letters form two separate pieces, and the comparative with its abbreviation sits in the gap between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of breath with anticipation or thrill is the condition of panting excitement the clue describes.

clue.text: Feeling nurse had on books about great healer

parts.note: SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade
from the saying that time is the great healer
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: An emotion a nurse experienced while reading books about a famous doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The great healer is not a doctor but time, from the proverb. The nurse sits on top, and the books are written about time.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is an emotion or attitude, so it serves as a synonym for a feeling.

clue.text: Book of songs accompanied by unknown old instrument

parts.note: a psalter is the book of Psalms
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A hymn book used alongside an obscure antique instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The psaltery is an ancient plucked stringed instrument, a kind of zither played in medieval times.

clue.text: Behave rashly with second girl, over spare diamonds

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a girl's name
on and over both mean upon or about
a spare figure is a lean one
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone is reckless with a second girlfriend, splashing out on spare diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: To skate on thin ice is the idiom for taking a risky course where things could give way at any moment.

clue.text: Crossing Maidenhead, a solitary social worker

indicators.note: crossing means spanning or straddling, so the solitary phrase goes round the letter

parts.note: a loner is a solitary person

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of maiden, read off the town's name

explanation.surface: A lonely care worker making a journey through the Berkshire town of Maidenhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidenhead is a Thames town west of London, but here it splits into Maiden and head.
explanation.definitionFit: An almoner was a hospital social worker in Britain, originally one who gave alms to the poor.

clue.text: School replacing English with a form of art

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of another in the word for school

parts.note: a college is a school
E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: A school drops English in favour of an art course.
explanation.definitionFit: Collage is an artwork made by gluing scraps of paper, fabric or photographs onto a surface.

clue.text: Keen to make an impression round king or queen

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the earlier words wrap about the royal letter

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a dent is a hollow impression
R stands for Rex or Regina, Latin king and queen

explanation.surface: Eager to impress a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The indefinite article and the dent together go round the royal letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate and enthusiastic, a close synonym of eager or keen.

clue.text: Extending indefinitely, it's fifty miles out

indicators.note: out here means wrong or not in place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's estimate of a long stretch is fifty miles off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without limits or bounds goes on endlessly, which is what extending indefinitely describes.

clue.text: Foreign character's articles about end of conflict

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the articles go round the letter

parts.note: the definite article the and the indefinite article a

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the last letter of conflict

explanation.surface: A foreigner's newspaper pieces on the closing stages of a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character from a non-English script.

clue.text: Learner in dire trouble?

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so the letters are put into disarray

parts.note: L is the learner plate abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student in deep difficulty, perhaps through not working.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a lazy student is a learner heading for dire trouble, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout who avoids work is the sort of pupil likely to land in serious difficulty at exam time.

clue.text: Chap's name I put in before

indicators.note: put in tells us to insert the preceding pieces into the word for earlier

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone recalls having entered a man's name earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for is, joining the definition to the wordplay; ERE splits round N and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a familiar male first name, so it can stand for a particular fellow.

clue.text: Go along with American writer and eat freely

parts.note: James Fenimore Cooper wrote The Last of the Mohicans

indicators.note: freely means without constraint, so the letters move about at will

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to keep company with an American author and dine without restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: To cooperate is to work together and comply, the same as going along with a plan or person.

clue.text: Eccentric Scotsman given a rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading the word from the bottom up

parts.note: Mac is a generic name for a Scotsman

explanation.surface: An odd Scot receives a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccentric looks like an adjective describing the Scot, but it is the engineering noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A cam is a rotating wheel or projection, and an eccentric is an off-centre wheel doing the same mechanical job.

clue.text: Enclosed area — a jolly place for swinging sailors once

parts.note: a yard is an enclosed piece of ground
taken as written
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A fenced space described as a cheerful spot where sailors used to have fun swinging.
explanation.walkthrough: Swinging sounds like play, but it means hanging: mutinous sailors were once hanged from the end of a ship's spar.
explanation.definitionFit: The yardarm is the outer end of a ship's yard, the spar from which offenders were hanged at sea.

clue.text: Implore opponents at table to negotiate

parts.note: East and North are opposing partnerships at the bridge table
to treat with someone is to negotiate terms

explanation.surface: Someone begs rivals across a table to come to terms.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge, North and South play against East and West, so any one of East and North are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or plead earnestly, the same as imploring someone.
